outputs.exact_statement:
For the field $\phi$ just specified, there exist $m_1,Z,\delta>0$ and a positive measure $\rho_{\mathrm{rest}}$ such that $$\rho=Z\delta_{m_1^2}+\rho_{\mathrm{rest}},
 \qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\rho_{\mathrm{rest}}\subset[(m_1+\delta)^2,\infty).
 \label{intro:atom}$$ In particular, $m_1$ is the smallest mass in the support of the spin-field two-point function.

There are integers $K_0,M_0>0$ and constants $c,C>0$ with the following properties. Write $w_k=M_0 2^k$, and let $Z_N(t,w)$ be the partition function on a torus of time length $t$ and spatial circumference $w$.* 1. *In the cutoff plane, all joint moments of the variables [inp:field] converge to those of the Euclidean field $\phi$. The limiting Schwinger distributions are tempered, Euclidean invariant, and $O(3)$ covariant. Their Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction is the Wightman field of Theorem 1, with unique vacuum $\Omega$ and $$H_{\mathrm{phys}}|_{\Omega^\perp}\ge m>0.$$ For some real test $f$ supported strictly in positive time, the one-field reflection norm $\mathbb E[\phi^1(\theta f)\phi^1(f)]$ is strictly positive.* 2. *For all $N\ge K_0$ and $k\ge0$, $$0\le \Delta_N(w_k) :=4\log Z_N(w_k,w_k)-\log Z_N(2w_k,2w_k) \le C e^{-c w_k}. \label{inp:defect}$$* 3. *On these square tori and on the cutoff plane, the component moment measures $$S_{r,N}^{\boldsymbol i} =(B_Na^2)^r\sum_{x_1,\ldots,x_r} \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j=1}^r q_{x_j}^{i_j}\right] \delta_{(x_1,\ldots,x_r)}$$ are nonnegative. For arbitrary translated unit boxes $Q_1,\ldots,Q_r$, $$S_{r,N}^{\boldsymbol i}(Q_1\times\cdots\times Q_r) \le C^r r!, \label{inp:majorant}$$ uniformly in $N\ge K_0$, the square torus, the box positions, and the component indices.

Fix finitely many real component test shapes of bounded support. Their arbitrary translates, in the cutoff plane or in the square tori of Proposition 2, satisfy $$\mathbb E|X_f^i|^r\le A^r r!,\qquad \mathbb Ee^{\kappa|X_f^i|}\le C \label{inp:tails-bound}$$ for some $A,C,\kappa>0$ independent of the cutoff, volume, and translations. The constants can also be chosen uniformly for test families of bounded supremum and support diameter. For each fixed $r$, tests supported in a common bounded set obey $$\|X_f^i-X_g^i\|_{L^r}\le C_r\|f-g\|_\infty, \label{inp:test-difference}$$ with the same uniformity under translations of that set.

For each $N\ge K_0$, define $P_N(t,w)=(tw)^{-1}\log Z_N(t,w)$ and $P_{\infty,N}=\inf_{t,w}P_N(t,w)$. There are constants $c,C>0$, independent of $N$, such that, whenever $\min(t,w)$ is sufficiently large, $$0\le P_N(t,w)-P_{\infty,N}
       \le Ce^{-c\min(t,w)}.
 \label{tra:pressure-bound}$$ If $g_N(w)=a^{-1}\log\lambda_{0,N}(w)-wP_{\infty,N}$, then $$0\le g_N(w)\le Cwe^{-cw},\qquad
 0\le\log R_{N,w}(t)\le Ctwe^{-c\min(t,w)}.
 \label{tra:trace}$$ The bound for $g_N$ holds at every sufficiently large allowed circumference.
There are $c_0>0$ and $w_0<\infty$ such that $$e_N(w)\ge c_0\qquad(N\ge K_0,\ w\ge w_0,\ w\in a_N\mathbb N).$$

One has $\|A_F\|\le\|F\|_\infty$. Write $\mathbb E_{\mathrm{cyl},N,w}F=\langle\Omega_{N,w},A_F\Omega_{N,w}\rangle$ for the infinite-time cylinder expectation. If $t>r$, then $$\left|\mathbb E_{\mathrm{tor},N;t,w}F
       -\mathbb E_{\mathrm{cyl},N,w}F\right|
 \le\|F\|_\infty
       \bigl(s_{N,w}(t-r)+s_{N,w}(t)\bigr).
 \label{tra:torus-cylinder}$$

Let $w=w_k$ be sufficiently large. If the support of a bounded observable $F$ has a lift contained in a rectangle of extent at most $3w/4$ in each coordinate, then $$\left|\mathbb E_{\mathrm{tor},N;w,w}F-\mathbb E_{\mathrm{plane},N}F\right|
       \le C\|F\|_\infty e^{-cw},
 \label{tra:plane-comparison}$$ uniformly in $N\ge K_0$. The assertion holds for bounded measurable observables. Comparison of this square with its infinite-time cylinder requires only the time extent bound.

Fix a number of component tests, chosen from families with uniformly bounded suprema and support diameters. If their translated supports together satisfy the extent condition of Proposition 8, then the square-torus and cutoff-plane expectations of their product differ by at most $Ce^{-cw}$. The constants may depend on the number and shapes of the tests but not on their separate translations, the cutoff, or $w$.

Let $P$ and $Q$ be monomials in spin components for the law [par:graph-law], of even total degrees $r$ and $s$, with nonempty site lists $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$. Put $$G=\max_{x\in\mathcal A,\ y\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E(q_x^3q_y^3).$$ There is a constant $C_{r,s}$, depending only on the two degrees, such that $$\label{par:quadratic-bound} |\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(P,Q)|\le C_{r,s}G^2.$$ If either monomial is constant, its covariance is zero.

The marginal law of $\alpha$ in [par:angles] is positively associated. For even-degree monomials each using a single component, covariances are nonnegative when the components agree and nonpositive when they differ. The same covariance signs hold for the two-component plane rotator.

Along the prescribed circumferences $w_k=M_0 2^k$, $$\label{vis:gap}
 \liminf_{k\to\infty}\;\liminf_{N\to\infty} e_N(w_k)\ge m_*.$$

There exist $\epsilon,c_0>0$ and fixed thresholds $N_0,w_0$ such that for $N\ge N_0$, $w=w_k\ge w_0$, and every center $s$, $$\label{vis:positive-weight}
 \mathbb P_{\mathrm{tor}}\{S(h_s,h'_s)\ge\epsilon\}\ge c_0.$$
